recommendation_summary: The reply recommends that nightly-sync write a success stamp when it finishes, that a 04:30 cron on edna send mail through the summary's mail path if today's stamp is missing, and that startup be wrapped so an exception also sends that mail with the error.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to stop finding a dead nightly-sync by accident. You suggested a central log on the Synology, Pieter Levels style, maybe all in Docker.
labels.Deleted: Central logging and a Docker stack. A log you will not open never wakes you, and Docker adds a host without adding a signal.
labels.Bottleneck: The only alert is the summary email, and it runs after startup. An expired token exits before that, and nothing treats a missing run as a failure.
labels.Checked myself: I used only what you just told me. I have not opened the script, cron, or the NAS.

note: This is a borderline case: the missing-stamp check alone would catch the startup crash, so the extra exception mail is a second alerting mechanism, which makes it LARGER rather than SMALL.
